lines.text: | **"the breath of life"** | 7: Gen 2:7; 6:17; 7:15, 22; Isa 57:16 … | life as given and held by God |
| "A tranquil heart gives life to the flesh, but envy makes the bones rot" | Pro 14:30 | the inner state giving life, or rotting the body |
| **"he is your life and length of days"** | Deu 30:20; also "Christ who is your life" (Col 3:4) | life named as a person, not only as a span |
| **"I have set before you life and death … choose life"** | Deu 30:19 | life and death as what the inner being chooses between |
| **"the path of life"** / "the way of life" | Psa 16:11; Pro 15:24; 5:6 / Pro 6:23; Jer 21:8 | life as a way walked |

| **"the fountain of life"** | Psa 36:9 ("with you is the fountain of life; in your light do we see light"); Pro 10:11; 13:14; 14:27; 16:22 | where life is drawn from: God, the mouth of the righteous, the teaching of the wise, the fear of the Lord, good sense |
| "the land of the living" | 14: Psa 27:13; 116:9; Eze 32 … | where life is lived before God |
| "he has put eternity into man's heart" | Ecc 3:11 | the heart made for more than a span |
| "teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom" | Psa 90:12 | the span of life teaching the heart |
| "In him we live and move and have our being"; "he himself gives to all mankind life and breath and everything" | Act 17:28, 25 | life and breath as given by God, in him |
| "What is your life? For you are a mist" | Jam 4:14 | life's brevity |
| "the valley of the shadow of death" | Psa 23:4 (+ 5 more) | death as a place walked through while living |
| "the way of all the earth"; "gathered to his people" | 1Ki 2:2; Jos 23:14 / Gen 25:8; 49:33 … | death as the end |
| **"passed from death to life"**; "newness of life"; "your life is hidden with Christ in God" | Joh 5:24; Rom 6:4; Col 3:3 | death as the place of a new beginning |

**Caution.** Pro 4:23 and Pro 14:30 *state* that life flows from the heart and that a tranquil heart gives life. "Life is the expression of the inner being" is the researcher's wording of the frame. In the text it would appear as **"I read"**, resting on those verses. It would not be presented as a statement Scripture makes in those words.

findings.text: Proposal: three layers, each with one job.: Ch 2 = the scene. For each movement it gives one coherent account of what Scripture says life and death are, using chosen verses (the 10.1 "Fear" model, #1930). Where a part belongs to an activity, Ch 2 states it briefly and points on, e.g. "Asking God for life is followed in 10.9".; The other chapters = the working. Where an activity is the subject, that chapter carries the full account and points back to Ch 2. Examples: asking for life → 10.9; choosing life → 10.7; turning and living → 10.7 / 14; wanting to die → 10.6; breathing out lies → 10.5; the heart that dies → 4; Each chapter also gets a short line where its subject meets life and death. This is how parts of Ch 2 "find their way into other chapters" without being lost from the scene.; The detail = the evidence layer, kept whole. Nothing is cut from the record: the overview data file, including the §3 cluster links; the unit ledgers; a new living linkage map, life-death-linkage-map.md; The map has one row per link: overview cluster link or ledger id → the chapter or section that now carries it → its status (carried / pointer only / not yet read). It is the bridge between the overview's rich detail and the narrative. OT-08 points to it. Every later strand adds its own life and death rows.; The first rows come from the overview's §3, e.g.: M12 righteousness (76 near verses) → 10.8 / Ch 2 B, "not yet read"; M47 inner seat (302) → Ch 4–8; M64 choosing (Deu 30:19) → 10.7, carried by LD-28
